questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The axolotl: a tropical lizard bred mainly as a pet in home aquariums
How the Aztecs drained Lake Texcoco and built the city of Tenochtitlan
The axolotl: a neotenic, regenerating, critically endangered salamander
Why tilapia and carp are raised commercially in the lakes of Xochimilco
questions.explain: It describes the axolotl's biology, endangered status, and remarkable regeneration.

questions.q: Which invasive species have driven wild axolotls near extinction?
options: Catfish and bass
Crayfish and eels
Bullfrogs and trout
Tilapia and carp
questions.explain: Wild axolotls have been driven near extinction by introduced tilapia and carp.

questions.q: Which structure is credited for initiating appendage growth in axolotls?
options: The apical ectodermal ridge and cap (AER/AEC)
The blastema forming under the wound epidermis
A system regulating macrophages and suppressing inflammation
The external gills and gill slits
questions.explain: The passage credits the apical ectodermal ridge (AER) with the apical ectodermal cap (AEC) for initiating appendage growth.

questions.q: What colour are albinistic axolotls' eyes?
options: Gold
Pink
Black
Red
questions.explain: Albinistic axolotls have a pale pink or white body with red eyes.

questions.q: What does the passage imply about axolotl regeneration and age?
options: It disappears entirely once the animal reaches sexual maturity
It declines with age but does not completely disappear
It is limited to the tail and the outer layers of skin
It stays constant throughout life, unaffected by age
questions.explain: The regenerative ability declines with age but does not completely disappear, and drops after metamorphosis.
